title: Rocket Lab Lands $266 Million Air Force Contract as Defense Wins Stack Up
excerpt: The launch company secured a firm-fixed-price deal for 12 suborbital missions using its HASTE rocket, days after being selected for a $17 billion Space Force program.
body:
• Rocket Lab secured a $266 million firm-fixed-price U.S. Air Force contract for 12 suborbital launches, with options for six additional missions through December 2028.
  • RKLB stock jumped 9 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement, after already gaining more than 5 percent during the regular session.
  • The contract is for HASTE (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron), a suborbital variant of Rocket Lab's proven Electron rocket used in hypersonic weapons testing.
  • The award came days after Rocket Lab was named one of seven companies eligible for the $17 billion National Security Space Launch Phase 3 Lane 1 program.

Rocket Lab USA secured a $266 million U.S. Air Force contract for suborbital launch services on Tuesday, sending shares up 9 percent in after-hours trading and adding to what has become one of the strongest defense contract pipelines in the commercial space sector.

The firm-fixed-price deal covers 12 suborbital launch vehicles with options for six additional launches. Work will be performed at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Alaska through December 31, 2028. The Air Force is obligating $112 million in fiscal 2025 research, development, test and evaluation funds at the time of award.

The contract was awarded through competitive acquisition, with three offers received and Space Systems Command serving as the contracting activity.

HASTE: The Hypersonic Edge

The award is specifically for HASTE — Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron — a suborbital variant of Rocket Lab's proven Electron rocket designed for hypersonic weapons testing. The contract builds on a prior $190 million award earlier this year, underscoring the Pentagon's accelerating investment in hypersonic capabilities.

"This is strong validation of HASTE's operational performance."

— Erik Rasmussen, Stifel analyst

Stifel analyst Erik Rasmussen noted the contract's rising strategic relevance as the U.S. accelerates hypersonic weapons development, maintaining a 'Buy' rating on Rocket Lab shares. Piper Sandler, which initiated coverage last week with a 'Neutral' rating and $83 price target, said Rocket Lab's Electron rocket offers an edge in small-payload launches versus SpaceX's Falcon 9.

Defense Momentum Builds

The contract win came just days after the U.S. Space Force announced that Rocket Lab and SpaceX were among seven companies awarded positions on the National Security Space Launch Phase 3 Lane 1 program, which carries a $17 billion ceiling for future launch services. Taken together, the awards position Rocket Lab as a leading player in the U.S. defense launch market alongside SpaceX.

The company's contracted backlog reached a record $2.2 billion following first-quarter results in May, when revenue climbed 63 percent year-over-year to $200.35 million. Rocket Lab also has a pending $8 billion acquisition of satellite operator Iridium, which would transform the company into a vertically integrated space services provider — though it introduces dilution concerns that have weighed on the stock.

Valuation Debate Intensifies

Despite the contract wins, Rocket Lab's valuation remains a point of contention. The stock trades at roughly 66 times trailing sales — an extraordinary multiple for a company that posted a net loss of $198 million on $601.8 million in fiscal 2025 revenue, with net margins of negative 27 percent.

RKLB shares have fallen 0.55 percent year-to-date but gained over 38 percent in the past 12 months. The stock closed at $69.99 on July 23, well below its all-time high, with earnings scheduled for August 6.

The broader space sector has been volatile since SpaceX's June IPO on the Nasdaq, with retail investors tracking whether the contract wins and upcoming Neutron rocket debut — CEO Peter Beck's most important milestone — can justify the premium valuation. SpaceX, meanwhile, has reportedly begun pulling back future Falcon 9 bookings beyond 2028, a shift that could benefit Rocket Lab as customers seek alternative launch providers.

What to Watch

Investors will be closely monitoring Rocket Lab's August 6 earnings report for updated guidance on the HASTE program, Neutron development timeline and Iridium acquisition progress. The Neutron rocket's debut later this year represents the single largest catalyst for the company's long-term thesis, opening a medium-lift market far larger than what the Electron platform has addressed.
